risks: Minimal: the project measures adherence to an existing guideline and changes how prescribing choices are prompted and discussed. The main risks are an animal that needs an HPCIA being delayed, which the prompt avoids by allowing any documented reason, and blame if clinic or individual data are shared; feedback is by clinic and anonymised.
consent: Owners are told through consult-room notices that the clinics are working to use antimicrobials more carefully; treatment decisions remain with the veterinary surgeon and the owner. Staff take part as part of normal work and no individual prescribing data are shown to others.
data: Weekly counts by drug class, species and clinic only; manual samples record consultation date, clinic and culture submission without owner names; data are kept on the group's restricted drive and deleted after the SQUIRE report.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: owners on low incomes are most affected by culture cost, and older owners or owners with disabilities may be unable to give tablets to a cat. Free culture during the cycles, nurse tablet-giving appointments and an injection option with a recorded reason protect these owners, and culture uptake is reported by clinic because the clinics serve areas with different incomes.
effectiveness: Success means a sustained shift in the HPCIA share with a stable amoxicillin-clavulanate share and no rise in 7-day re-consultation; a failed balancing measure leads to a revised cycle, not a claim of success.
efficiency: About 15 minutes of report time a week, two hours of sampling a month and existing meeting time; free culture is already budgeted.
costs: Free culture for two months within the existing budget, printing of guides, and staff time within normal hours.
grants: None needed; a veterinary stewardship award could fund spread to partner practices.
partnerships: Practice manager (weekly report), head nurse (sampling and tablet-giving appointments), software administrator (prompt), and two owner representatives from the clinics' client panel (wording of notices and handouts).
rebPath: Classified by the group's clinical governance committee as quality improvement not requiring ethical review (CGC-2026-031); no animal undergoes any procedure outside normal care, so no animal ethics committee review is needed. A later publication follows SQUIRE 2.0.
limitations: Four clinics in one group, no concurrent comparison, and an outcome measure that is a prescribing process rather than animal health.
summary: Minimal-risk QI with clinic-level feedback, protection for owners facing cost or tablet difficulty, and a completed governance classification.
